newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan engineers and state resolve pay dispute.
newsitem.headline: Jordan engineers and state resolve pay dispute.

text.p: Jordan's Islamist dominated engineers union called off a campaign of strike action after the government pledged to resolve long simmering pay demands, union leaders said on Saturday.

Union officials in the Jordanian Engineers Association said Prime Minister Abdul Karim al-Kabariti gave his approval to an understanding reached on Friday with the government that pledged to resolve key pay demands for 4,000 public sector members.
"I believe the government was responsive to the injustice that has befallen the engineers and in the demands to get their rights," Hosni Abu Ghaida, deputy head of the engineers union, told Reuters.
The accord set up a joint committee to meet and agree within three months to a key demand for nearly 20 percent rises in salaries of around 4,000 public sector engineers.
Bonus allowances were agreed to and would have an immediate effect, union leaders said.
The Islamist dominated union, with a total of 26,000 members who are mainly private sector engineers, is by far the country's largest and most powerful union.
Unionists say starting salaries for graduates -- 270 dinars ($381) for general practioners, 400 dinars for specialist doctors and 215 dinars for graduate engineers -- are too low.
The doctors association, with a 11,000 strong membership, is also threatening strike action on October 26, calling for similar pay demands for its 2,800 public-sector colleagues, union sources said.
Other professional unions, including dentists, nurses and geologists, are also raising their voices over pay demands.

Public sector employees who form nearly half an estimated 900,000 workforce complain that annual salary rises of well under 10 percent in the last few years have fallen far behind consumer price hikes.
Steep bread price hikes last August that sparked civil unrest are blamed by many Jordanians for having a spiral effect on a long list of basic consumer items.
